HeyGluco was born from a family’s own experience with type 1 diabetes. After their daughter Ecaterina was diagnosed at seven, they found themselves navigating a new reality filled with medical information, calculations, uncertainty and a lot of fear. What they needed most in those first months wasn’t more information, but a clearer, more human way to make sense of it.They decided to create the resource they wished they had from day one: a place where families could learn, find practical tools and feel supported by people who had already been through the same experience. Our challenge was to turn that deeply personal idea into a brand that could talk about a serious subject with clarity and empathy, without feeling clinical or intimidating.

LP:One Motor was born from the ambition to build high-performance cars in Romania, bringing the raw experience of motorsport closer to the road. Its first models were conceived around lightweight construction, performance and a more direct connection between driver and machine.The challenge was to create a brand capable of standing alongside established names in performance automotive, while expressing the precision and engineering behind a company equally at home on the racetrack and on the road.
Less size, more scope

MVP Agency was created to connect top sports talent with brands through long-term partnerships, campaigns and sponsorships. The ambition goes beyond traditional athlete representation, positioning its talent as ambassadors, creators and personalities with a presence beyond competition.The challenge was to build a brand that could carry the energy and confidence of sport without looking like a traditional sports identity, while giving a growing and diverse roster of talent the space to stand out.

Merci is an éclair brand from Barcelona built around a quieter take on indulgence. With a focus on craftsmanship, high-quality ingredients and refined flavours, the idea was to create a premium experience that feels considered and approachable rather than extravagant.The challenge was to translate that philosophy into a brand that could feel distinctly connected to Barcelona while keeping the calm, minimal character at the heart of Merci.

Munchies & Cream was created as an ice cream brand for people looking for something a little less predictable. With bold flavours, limited drops and a strong connection to food culture, the ambition was to build something people could follow, collect and talk about, not just pick from a freezer.The challenge was to give the brand a recognizable personality from day one, while leaving enough room for it to constantly change with new flavours, products and ideas.

One detail gave us the starting point for the entire identity: every YumYum recipe uses grape juice as its base, no matter the flavour. We turned that constant into the brand’s most recognizable element, creating a Y-shaped mark that also reads as a simplified grape.The rest of the identity was designed around the same idea of simplicity. A restrained visual system, distinctive typography and a refined colour palette give YumYum a contemporary feel while keeping the ingredients and product at the centre. The result is a brand that feels fresh and considered, with enough flexibility to live across packaging, digital and everything in between.

Tanti Maria is a delicatessen in Bucharest’s iconic Obor Market, built around carefully selected cured meats, cheeses and specialty products. The idea was to offer better quality without making the experience feel exclusive or out of place in a market known for its energy, familiarity and tradition.The challenge was to create a contemporary brand that still felt like it belonged in Obor, drawing on the nostalgia and familiarity behind the name Tanti Maria.

The Bagel Bar started with a simple idea: bring proper bagels to Bucharest and build a place with its own culture around them. More than a quick bite, it was meant to become a neighbourhood spot people could return to for the food, the atmosphere and everything happening around it.The challenge was to give a relatively unfamiliar product a strong, recognizable presence while building a brand that could feel just as natural on a bagel wrapper as it did on the storefront, a T-shirt or a Friday night poster.

WE’VE GOT RANGE
We believe creative work needs focus. That’s why we keep our team tight and our involvement high, so every project gets our full attention. We build brands from scratch or make them better.

We brought Tanti Maria to life as the face of the brand, inspired by that familiar aunt we somehow all know: warm, welcoming and always associated with good food. The illustrated character became the centre of an identity designed to feel instantly recognizable and personal.Bold, retro-inspired typography and a vibrant graphic system bring that nostalgia into the present without making the brand feel old-fashioned. The result is an identity rooted in the character of Obor, but built to work naturally across the store, packaging, merchandise and communication.

We built HeyGluco around the idea of making diabetes easier to understand and less frightening, especially for children. At the centre of the identity is Gluco, a small dragon designed as a familiar companion through a world of sensors, insulin, glucose levels and new routines.Every detail has a purpose. His three coloured spikes reference glucose levels, while the scarf is inspired by the international symbol of diabetes. Around him, we created a cast of characters based on everyday diabetes tools, turning unfamiliar medical objects into something children can recognise and relate to. A second, more narrative illustration style helps tell the family’s real story with more emotion and nuance.A warm, colourful palette moves away from the cold visual codes of healthcare, while typography and a clear editorial system make complex information easier to navigate. Together, they give HeyGluco a visual language that can educate without overwhelming and support without talking down.

We built LP:One around a visual language that feels engineered rather than decorated. Sharp typography, strong contrasts and a restrained graphic system reflect the precision and performance behind the cars, while giving the brand the confidence expected from the super sports category.The identity was designed to move between two sides of LP:One: motorsport and road-going performance. From the cars and racing applications to digital, communication and brand materials, the system creates one consistent world around the idea that performance should still feel visceral.

We built the identity around a symbol that brings together three parts of the Merci story. The letter M forms the foundation of the mark, a star at its centre represents craftsmanship, while the surrounding geometry takes inspiration from Barcelona’s stained glass windows.That idea extends into a restrained visual system where typography, warm tones and generous space let the product take the lead. The result is an identity that feels refined without becoming pretentious.

We built the identity around the product itself. The logomark combines the initials of Bagel Bar with the circular shape of a bagel hidden in the negative space, creating a compact symbol that can live almost anywhere.From there, we developed a bold visual and verbal language built around oversized typography, electric blue and playful graphics, paired with photography that keeps the food and the people around it feeling real. Lines like “Known by few, loved by you” gave the brand a voice of its own, while a flexible set of graphics allowed it to move beyond the menu into packaging, merchandise, social content and events.The result is a brand that feels less like a conventional food spot and more like the world built around The Bagel Bar.

From packaging and social content to merchandise and limited drops, every new application becomes another opportunity to expand the Munchies & Cream universe.
